o:
A subarray is centered if its sum equals at least one element inside it. With n ≤ 500, an O(n²) enumeration over all subarrays is expected: fix the left endpoint, extend the right endpoint while maintaining the running sum and a hash set of elements currently in the window; the subarray is centered iff the running sum is in the set. A brute-force O(n³) version (recomputing the set per subarray) also passes but is wasteful.

Example 1: [-1,1,0] — three singles qualify; [1,0] has sum 1 present; [-1,1,0] has sum 0 present → 5. Example 2: [2,-3] — sums of length-2 windows (−1) match no element, so only the two singles count.
k: Fix left endpoint and sweep right, maintaining sum and member set incrementally
Centered ⟺ window sum ∈ set of window elements
n ≤ 500 ⇒ O(n²) with O(1) incremental updates is the target complexity

a.i: For every (l, r) pair, compute the sum and scan the window for an element equal to it. Straightforward and clearly correct; O(n³) is acceptable at n = 500 (≈ 2·10⁷ operations).
s: For each l, for each r ≥ l: compute window sum and check membership by scanning
Increment ans when the sum matches some element
a.t: O(n³) — all subarrays scanned with an inner membership scan

a.n: Approach 2: Incremental Sweep with Hash Set
a.i: Fix l and grow r. Keep the running sum and a set of window elements; both update in O(1) per step, so checking 'sum in set' makes the whole algorithm O(n²).
s: For each l: sum = 0, seen = empty set
For r from l to n−1: add nums[r] to sum and seen; if sum in seen, ans++
a.t: O(n²) — each (l, r) pair processed with O(1) average updates
a.sp: O(n) — the window set for one left endpoint

w: Present the O(n²) sweep as the main solution and mention the brute force only as a stepping stone. Pitfalls: forgetting that single-element subarrays are automatically centered (their sum equals the element), and 32-bit overflow of window sums (up to 500·1e5 = 5·10⁷ fits in int, but use 64-bit out of habit for safety with negatives). Follow-up: n up to 1e5 requires randomized hashing or bitset tricks over prefix sums, or counting centered subarrays with sum equal to a specific element.
